chose: python SQL context is read off the f-string's own text (a SQL statement shape: select…from / insert into / …), not off a quote-wrap around the interpolation
over: mirroring the JS "${expr}" double-quote signal literally (only flagging "{expr}" inside the literal)
flagging every f-string interpolation regardless of context
because: the f-string's delimiters consume the quotes that carry the JS signal, so a literal mirror would miss f"select * from {table}" — the canonical python sink; and context-free flagging is the wall-of-candidates failure the module header forbids. Verb-pair shapes (select…from, insert into) keep 'hello from {name}' out.

chose: skipped str.format, %-formatting, and multi-line triple-quoted f-strings on the python path
over: parsing .format(args)/% right-operands to pair placeholders with expressions
a cross-line state machine for f"""…""" blocks
because: the safe regexes grade the interpolated EXPRESSION; in .format/% the expression lives outside the literal, so a line regex would pin '{}' or '%s' as the site with nothing honest to grade — not nearly free, and precision over recall. Multi-line f-strings: the scanner is line-based and the python path follows its grain; a state machine breaks per-line addressing (line numbers, comment skips) for one idiom.

chose: python sites reuse the JS context labels sql-ident/html-value and the same Finding shape
because: site identity is context|file|expr — the .py path already separates them from TS sites, so a new namespace would only fork reconcile's move-invariant address and the report's two counters for zero added discrimination; reusing the labels makes relocation/duplication mechanics and safeSql/safeHtml application provably identical by construction
